messages.content:
Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime, every nonzero residue has a multiplicative inverse.

First note that no term can be \(396\), because then
\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2\equiv 0 \pmod{397},
\]
which cannot equal \(a_n\equiv 396\).
Also, no term can be \(0\): if \(a_n=0\) for some \(n>0\), then the recurrence at index \(n-1\) gives \(a_{n-1}\equiv 0\), and repeating backward would force \(a_0=0\), contradiction.

Thus all \(a_n\) are invertible modulo \(397\). Define
\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]
From
\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2\equiv a_n \pmod{397},
\]
we get
\[
a_{n+1}^{-1}\equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
= a_n+2+a_n^{-1}.
\]
Therefore
\[
b_{n+1}\equiv a_n+2+b_n \pmod{397},
\]
so
\[
a_n\equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2 \pmod{397}.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\), the \(b_n\) terms telescope:
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027 \pmod{397}.
\]

We have \(a_0=1\), so \(b_0=1\). Also \(a_{2026}=9\), so
\[
b_{2027}\equiv a_{2026}+2+b_{2026}
\equiv 11+9^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]
Since
\[
9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1 \pmod{397},
\]
we have
\[
9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353 \pmod{397}.
\]
Thus
\[
b_{2027}\equiv 11+353=364 \pmod{397}.
\]

Now
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-4054
= -3691 \pmod{397}.
\]
Since
\[
-3691+10\cdot 397=279,
\]
the desired remainder is

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
